mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% over two consecutive quarters signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 3% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO is below its 12-month MA for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% over two months signals a policy-induced disinflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases while CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated surge in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months signals robust demand expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 12-month MA and HOUST > 12-month MA for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when both GDPC1 and HOUST exceed their 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals labor market strength, which supports consumer demand and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months.
